newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts say SBC slowdown no surprise.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say SBC slowdown no surprise.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corporation (SBC) caused no surprise by announcing that earnings growth slowed in the third quarter of 1996 as world financial markets calmed down from a hectic first half, analysts said.

Most analysts said they would maintain forecasts for 1996 or set them slightly lower after SBC's nine-month report said net profit for the year would be "some percentage points" lower than earlier estimates.
SBC said ordinary net profit growth fell to 27 percent for nine months from 36 percent in the first half of this year.

Analyst Madeleine Hofmann at CS Research said slower world markets had been expected in the second half and would affect all big banks, which have extensive activities in trading on their own account and for customers.
"This is not a surprise and not a disappointment," she told Reuters.
"This is similar to what UBS reported," she aded.
SBC's rival Union Bank of Switzerland last week said nine month results were higher than a year ago but that third quarter earnings lagged a strong first half. It gave no absolute numbers.
Claudia von Tuerk at Pictet & Cie said she had expected a weaker third quarter compared to the first six months.
But she said she would now fine-tune her forecast for 1996 net profit by slightly shaving a current estimate of 1.375 billion Swiss francs.
"SBC seems to be a bit more cautious on net profit than they were in September." she said.
SBC predicted in September that ordinary net profit would total 1.4 billion Swiss francs before 3.3 billion in extraordiniary restructuring costs for a net loss of 1.9 billion.
Union Bank of Switzerland analyst Thomas Kalbermatten said the nine-month results were very positive despite the expected slowdown.
"This fits into my forecast of ordinary net profit after taxes at 1.37 billion (Swiss francs) before extraordinary restructuring costs," he said.

John Leonard at Salomon Brothers in London said that based on the SBC's commentary, he estimated third quarter net profit at between 350 million and 370 million Swiss francs as against an average of just under 500 million per quarter in the first half.
Leonard said he would now lower his estimate for 1996 net profit to around 1.3 billion Swiss francs from 1.4 billion.
"There was no great surprise but it was below my expectations for the second half of this year," he said about the statement.
